facts.statement: Psephosauriscus was an extinct genus of placodont reptile that lived during the Middle Triassic in Israel and Egypt.
facts.quote: Psephosauriscus is an extinct genus of placodont reptile from the Middle Triassic of Israel and Egypt.

facts.statement: The animal is known from bony armor plates found at Makhtesh Ramon in the Negev desert and Araif en Naqua on the Sinai Peninsula.
facts.quote: It is known from bony armor plates that have been found from Makhtesh Ramon in Israel's Negev desert and Araif en Naqua on Egypt's Sinai Peninsula.

facts.statement: Swedish paleontologist F. Brotzen described armor from Makhtesh Ramon in 1957, naming the species Psephosaurus mosis and Psephosaurus picardi.
facts.quote: Swedish paleontologist F. Brotzen described placodont armor from Makhtesh Ramon in 1957, naming the species Psephosaurus mosis and Psephosaurus picardi from the Beneckeia and Ceratites beds, respectively.

facts.statement: Austrian paleontologist Georg Haas named the species P. sinaiticus and P. rhombifer in 1959.
facts.quote: In 1959, Austrian paleontologist Georg Haas named P. sinaiticus and P. rhombifer from Araif en Naqua.

facts.statement: Fossils come from the Beneckeia beds of the Anisian stage and the Ceratites beds spanning the end of the Anisian and beginning of the Ladinian stages.
facts.quote: The Beneckeia beds date back to the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic, and the Ceratites beds date back to the end of the Anisian and beginning of the Ladinian stage.

facts.statement: Armor is abundant in Middle Triassic limestone in the Sinai and Negev regions, comparable to the Muschelkalk of Europe.
facts.quote: Armor of Psephosauriscus is abundant in Middle Triassic limestone in the Sinai and Negev regions, which is comparable to the Muschelkalk of European rock sequences.

facts.statement: The type species P. mosis is known from a single specimen containing portions of the carapace and plastron.
facts.quote: The type species of Psephosauriscus, P. mosis, is known from a single specimen including portions of the carapace and plastron.

facts.statement: The scutes covering the armor plates have less defined shapes than the hexagonal osteoderms beneath them.
facts.quote: The scutes that cover the armor plates do not have as well-defined a shape as the hexagonal osteoderms that lay underneath them.

facts.statement: Some osteoderms possess a raised keel.
facts.quote: Some osteoderms have a raised keel.

facts.statement: The species P. ramonensis is known from a partial carapace and a connected plastron.
facts.quote: P. ramonensis is known from a partial carapace and connected plastron.

facts.statement: The carapace osteoderms of P. ramonensis have smoother edges and lack the keel found in species like P. mosis.
facts.quote: The osteoderms of the carapace have smoother edges than most other species of Psephosauriscus, and lack the keel of species like P. mosis.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of P. sinaiticus are smaller than those of other species.
facts.quote: The osteoderms of the carapace and plastron are smaller than those of other species.

facts.statement: P. cf. rhombifer is distinguished from other species by the rectangular shape of its scutes.
facts.quote: P. cf. rhombifer can be distinguished from the three other species of Psephosauriscus by the rectangular shape of its scutes.

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the parent group Cyamodontoidea.
The animal is classified in the class Reptilia.
It is debated whether P. rhombifer belongs to Psephosauriscus because the original holotype specimen described by Haas was lost.
facts.quote: However, P. rhombifer could not be assigned with certainty to Psephosauriscus because the holotype specimen described by Haas had since been lost.

facts.statement: Rieppel tentatively described P. cf. rhombifer based on additional material from Araif en Naqua that showed similarities to other Psephosauriscus species.
facts.quote: Rieppel reported additional material from Araif en Naqua that showed similarities to P. rhombifer and the species of Psephosauriscus, which he tentatively described as a species within Psephosauriscus, Psephosauriscus cf. rhombifer.

rejected.statement: The genus was established in 2002 as a replacement name for several species previously assigned to the genus Psephosaurus.
rejected.quote: The genus was erected in 2002 as a replacement name for several species of the genus Psephosaurus, which was named in 1957.
